title: Migration Roadmap Mini-Deck for Platform Teams (Draft)
content:
Purpose: one-pager mini-deck to equip platform/infra leads and sellers with a concise, technical-first migration roadmap from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private. Focus is pragmatic steps, acceptance criteria, and common gating risks we see in early adopter conversions.

Audience: platform engineering leads, solution engineers, AE technical champions, customer SREs.

Slide 1 — Why this matters (30s opener)
- Migration is not just 'lift and shift' — it's an operational change: qos, capacity planning, and security controls.
- Quick stat to use with customers: typical latency reduction of 15–40% post-dedicated for production workloads (source: internal perf bench Q3 2025).
- Seller hook: Lower total cost per 1M tokens by ~25% at steady state after batching/kv-cache tuning.

Speaker note: start with the business upside (latency + cost) then pivot to the engineering checklist. Keep it short.

Slide 2 — High-level phases (visual: 4 boxes)
1) Discovery & Constraints (1–3 weeks)
2) Pilot (2–6 weeks)
3) Canary / Partial Traffic (1–4 weeks)
4) Scale & Operationalize (ongoing)

Bullet bullets: what each phase produces (artifact examples)
- Discovery: perf profile, expected token mix, regulatory constraints, network topology diagram, PCI/PII gating list.
- Pilot: dedicated GPU sizing runbook, canary playbook, baseline eval set.
- Canary: rollback thresholds, rollback automation (feature flags), observability dashboards.
- Scale: autoscaling policy, cost guardrails, runbook handoff to ops.

Slide 3 — Discovery checklist (detailed)
- Traffic characterization: request size distribution (tokens), model family, concurrency patterns.
- SLA targets: p50/p95/p99 latency targets, throughput (tokens/sec) per route.
- Data residency & encryption requirements (KMS/HSM).
- Compatibility constraints: GPU type availability, quantization tolerance, custom kernels.
- Ops constraints: maintenance windows, egress limits, VPC peering requirements.

Quick tip: ask for a sample of 48 hours of real request payloads (anonymized) — our estimators use that to recommend batching/kv-cache settings.

Slide 4 — Pilot playbook (practical recipe)
- Step 0: baseline on Hosted for 48-72h with prod-like load (collect p95, error rates, token profile).
- Step 1: provision 1–2 dedicated nodes (same model family) with conservative batch settings.
- Step 2: run synthetic and traffic-replay tests at 25/50/75/100% of expected concurrency. Capture perf and cache hit rates.
- Step 3: run quality regression checks on golden prompt set (evals) — track perplexity/embedding drift/semantic diffs.
- Step 4: cost modeling: projected monthly cost (tokens + infra) and threshold triggers for autoscale.

Notes: Include hooks to Redwood Optimize recommendations — quantization profile suggestions and batching hints.

Slide 5 — Canary and rollbacks (ops safe)
- Canary duration: min 72h at meaningful traffic slice (>5–10% depending on criticality).
- Key signals to monitor: token latency p95, tail latency p99, rate of generation errors, hallucination regression on eval set.
- Automated rollback triggers: >20% increase in p95 latency, >2x error rate, or quality regression beyond agreed threshold.
- Fallbacks: transparent model variant downgrade (lower memory model), route to Hosted, or temporary capacity bump.

Playbook snippet: "If p95 increases by 25% on canary for >30m, shift canary back to Hosted and open an incident with infra/engineering."

Slide 6 — Operational handoff (SRE runbook items)
- Dashboard checklist: per-route token/sec, cost-per-token, cache hit ratio, kernel GPU saturation metrics.
- Alerts: Sustained CPU/GPU saturation, queueing latency > X ms, model OOMs, KMS errors.
- Runbook links: incident runbook, on-call rotation schedule, scheduled maintenance process.

Slide 7 — Risk matrix (common customer objections)
- Concern: "We need strict data residency and KMS integration." Response: private deployments + HSM/KMS integrations documented; propose a staged KMS onboarding during pilot.
- Concern: "Dedicated will be too expensive for peak spikes." Response: autoscaling + burst capacity with fallback routing to Hosted. Show cost vs. SLA trade-off examples.
- Concern: "We have specialized models/custom kernels." Response: early compatibility validation in Discovery; custom runtime bundles supported in Private with enterprise engineering.

Slide 8 — Example timeline (real example from a 2025 migration)
- Week 0–2: Discovery (collected traffic, constraint doc)
- Week 3–6: Pilot (2 nodes, 3 synthetic tests, 1 customer quality review)
- Week 7–9: Canary (10% traffic -> 50% traffic) with rollback policy
- Week 10–12: Scale and policy automation

Callout: this example was for a fintech customer with p95 SLA of 400ms and strong PII constraints; we used Dedicated + VPC peering + KMS.

Slide 9 — Acceptance criteria (concrete)
- Perf: p95 latency <= baseline target (within +/-10%) under expected concurrency.
- Quality: no regression > 2% on golden eval set for top-level intent accuracy.
- Cost: steady-state cost per 1M tokens within agreed budget +/-15%.
- Ops: runbook validated, alerts tested, and on-call assigned.

Slide 10 — Playbook artifacts to deliver (attachments)
- Sizing workbook (sheet)
- Canary playbook (runbook doc)
- Eval prompt set + regression harness (repo link)
- Security checklist (compliance items)

Slide 11 — Example seller script (60s)
- "We typically run a short discovery to map your request profile, then a pilot so you can see real latency and cost benefits with minimal disruption. If you have residency or kernel constraints, we validate those up front and can start with a VPC-connected pilot. The engineering team handles the canary and we provide the rollback automations so you’re never more at-risk than you are on Hosted."

Speaker note: this is intentionally concise — hand to AE + SE for rehearsed delivery.

Slide 12 — Open questions / TODOs (draft, internal)
- TODO: get up-to-date cost model from Finance for Dedicated instances (contact: Ben K.).
- TODO: instrument default golden eval set for new release candidates (owner: Applied ML).
- Open question: acceptable minimum canary traffic % for regulated customers? Need legal input.
- TODO: add concrete example of autoscale policy JSON for platform teams (engineering to provide template).

Appendix A — Short glossary
- KV-cache: key-value prefix cache for reducing recompute on repeated prompts.
- Canary: partial traffic routing to new infra to validate behavior.
- Quantization profile: model weight compression settings that affect perf and quality.

Appendix B — Links and refs
- Confluence migration playbook: CONFLUENCE-PLT-8472
- Jira plan ticket: JIRA-INF-3421 (pilot tracking)
- Example PR for config templates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prod-configs/pull/256

Notes for reviewers:
- This is a compact, technical-first deck. Aim is to be usable as a 10–12 slide deck or as a one-page cheat sheet for SEs.
- Feedback requested: add or prune items in discovery checklist, and confirm acceptance criteria thresholds with Applied ML and Finance.
- Style note: keep slides short, provide links to longer runbooks rather than embedding everything.

Draft history: created 2025-11-02 by Maya Chen; iterated with SEs in Dec 2025; last major edit 2026-02-20 (added acceptance criteria and risk matrix).
